clue.text: After loose scrum, dismiss pack on one's back

indicators.note: after says the dismissal piece follows the scrum piece in the answer

parts.note: a ruck is rugby's loose scrum, formed over a ball on the ground
to sack someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: A rugby coach, after a messy scrum, drops a player and sends them packing.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruck is a rugby term: players bind over a loose ball on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the shoulders by hikers, a backpack.

clue.text: Party seen to be in contravention

indicators.note: seen to be in means the answer sits inside the following word's letters

explanation.surface: A party held against the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large dance party, often all-night.

clue.text: One who imitates leaders of PETA yet chooses to wear fur?

indicators.note: to wear puts the leading letters within the fur garment, as a body inside a coat

parts.note: a fur is a coat made of animal fur

indicators.note: leaders of takes the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An imitator: the animal-rights group PETA, yet choosing to wear fur?
explanation.walkthrough: PETA is the animal-rights group People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, famously against fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is someone who slavishly copies others' behaviour.

clue.text: Salad plant to reveal unexpectedly to big cat, first off

parts.note: to spring something on someone is to surprise them with it

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter of the cat word is dropped

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A salad vegetable sprung as a surprise on a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring onion is a young onion with a long green stalk, eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Rising volume with air conditioning that makes puss go mad?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a pint is a measure of volume

explanation.surface: A rising noise level and an air conditioner that drive the cat crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests loudness, but here it is a liquid measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Catnip is a plant of the mint family whose scent excites domestic cats.

clue.text: Location that's superb when going back

indicators.note: going back tells us to read the word for superb from right to left

parts.note: tops is slang for excellent or superb

explanation.surface: A place that's wonderful to return to.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular place or site, a synonym of location.

clue.text: Sudden anxiety with satyr-like character in charge

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god with goat legs and horns, like a satyr

explanation.surface: Abrupt fear in the presence of a goat-like being who runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself comes from Pan, said to cause sudden terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a sudden overwhelming fear or alarm.

clue.text: Special gift almost certainly something valuable

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the gift word is lost

parts.note: a treat is a special present or indulgence
sure is used as an affirmative meaning certainly

explanation.surface: A special present that is almost certainly something precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is wealth or a precious object, anything highly prized.

clue.text: Spiteful person used to remove vetness from vindscreen?

indicators.note: the clue's own mock-accented spellings, with V where W belongs, tell us to do the same swap

parts.note: a wiper is the device used to clear wetness from a windscreen

explanation.surface: A comic accent asks for the thing that clears rain from a car's windscreen.
explanation.walkthrough: The device is a WIPER; spoken in the same stage accent that turns wetness into 'vetness', its W also becomes V.
explanation.definitionFit: Viper is used figuratively for a malicious, treacherous person, after the venomous snake.

clue.text: Crush half of troy weight

indicators.note: half of takes just the first two of the four letters of troy

parts.note: an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A command to grind down a troy-weight measure by half.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy weight is the system used for precious metals; here 'troy' and 'weight' split into separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to beat them heavily, to crush them in a contest.

clue.text: Person in theatre who performs surgery using rubber and ruler

parts.note: op is short for operation, surgery
a rubber is a pencil eraser, so using it means erasing
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a queen, a ruler

explanation.surface: A theatre worker who operates using a rubber and a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' and 'surgery' point to an operating theatre; the definition's theatre is the opera house. In Britain a rubber is a pencil eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera singer sings roles on stage in operas, a stage performer.

clue.text: Criminal handlers of stolen goods keeping identification secrets

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal

indicators.note: keeping means the handlers hold the identification letters within them

parts.note: fences are people who receive and sell stolen property

explanation.surface: Crooked dealers in stolen goods are carrying ID and private information.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidences are private matters told in trust, i.e. secrets shared with someone.

clue.text: Tart crumbled in officers' dining room makes a soft base

indicators.note: in places the rearranged pastry letters inside the dining room

parts.note: a mess is where military officers eat

indicators.note: crumbled says the letters of the pastry word are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tart crumbles in the officers' mess, providing something soft underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry being served in the mess, but it is only anagram fodder; 'crumbled' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is the padded base of a bed, soft to lie on.

clue.text: Someone who writes in French, to the Thunderer?

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A writer addresses a letter, in French, to the Thunderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' is also a nickname of The Times newspaper, which suits a writer, but here it is the god Thor.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is a writer of books or other works.

clue.text: Hairdresser: one supplying insults?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as one who deals in barbs, cutting remarks

explanation.surface: A hairdresser who is also free with the insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbs are pointed insults, so a jokey 'barb-er' hands them out; separately it names a men's hairdresser.

clue.text: Variant of Belgian language

indicators.note: variant of says to produce another arrangement of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: A form of Belgian speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language spoken in Bangladesh and West Bengal in India.

clue.text: Moan about feeble National Trust

parts.note: lame means weak or unconvincing, feeble

explanation.surface: Complaining about a weak National Trust.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament something is to mourn or complain about it.

clue.text: Technical word island country used for "ending"

parts.note: a term is a word with a specialist or technical meaning
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A jargon word on an island nation is used to mean 'ending'.
explanation.definitionFit: A termination is a finish or conclusion, so it means the close or end of something.

clue.text: Tear wrapping from éclair that's readier to eat

parts.note: to rip is to tear

indicators.note: wrapping from takes the outside letters of the pastry word

explanation.surface: Ripping the wrapper off a cream cake that is more ready to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Riper fruit has matured further, so is more ready for eating.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge sample from Golden Years

indicators.note: sample from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Refusing to recognise a taste of one's golden years.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny something is to refuse to admit or recognise it.

clue.text: Former partner strongly criticises European extension

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
pans means slates or harshly reviews

explanation.surface: An ex harshly criticises a European's planned extension.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch or area, an extent of space.

clue.text: Little fruit from Greek imitator

parts.note: an ape is someone who mimics, from the verb to ape

explanation.surface: A small fruit supplied by a Greek copycat.
explanation.definitionFit: A grape is a small berry that grows in bunches on a vine.

clue.text: The type to put in an order

explanation.surface: A kind of person to arrange things neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a kind or category; as a verb it means arrange by class.

clue.text: Change in entirety, for all time

indicators.note: change in tells us to rearrange the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Something altered wholly, once and forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, time without beginning or end.
